subject.title: feat(self-host): local console sign-in without Cloudflare Access

question: Should the Docker self-host profile officially support an opt-in browser console session authenticated by the existing shared admin token?
rationale: The patch is intentionally additive and includes a security-conscious implementation, but deciding whether this local browser-session model belongs in the supported self-host product cannot be resolved from tests or code review alone.

options.title: Sponsor opt-in local sessions
options.body: Accept the disabled-by-default local-auth mode as the supported self-host console path, with the documented shared-admin and per-isolate rate-limit constraints.

options.title: Keep the API-only profile
options.body: Retain the current self-host boundary and decline browser-session support until a different authentication model is approved.

recommendation.title: Sponsor opt-in local sessions
recommendation.body: Accept the disabled-by-default local-auth mode as the supported self-host console path, with the documented shared-admin and per-isolate rate-limit constraints.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged self-host profile established the current API-only contract and described this exact capability as a potential future follow-up.
